questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I always wanted to experience the US and I have heard good things about University of California.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I can really recommend Santa Barbara. Especially if you are interested in learning to surf, hiking and other outdoor activities. Nature is always close to you. You can go for a run on the beach before class and sit at the library with view over the ocean.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fine. I received an e-mail with information from the advisor at USCB just before I arrived and one more after arriving. If I needed more information, it was possible to call the advisor or write an e-mail.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was assigned to two different groups one with two other international students also arriving the same time as me and another group with American students from UCSB who are going on exchange to Denmark the following semester. It was very helpful to have other people to discuss things with and learn from. Otherwise, as I mentioned before it was possible to call or send an email to the office or advisor of UCSB Education Abroad Program.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It is easy to find information or clarify any concerns.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
I looked at the different types of housing on campus at:
www.housing.ucsb.edu
It is the more expensive option compared to renting a room privately. It includes some meals at the dining hall, which is very easy and carefree to be able to just go to the dining hall for breakfast, lunch and dinner. There are not many single rooms, mostly it is a double or triple room. I lived with to other girls. I ended up liking it much. We could look after each other and they were able to help me with a lot of practical things.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There are several dining halls on campus and one a little away from campus. I chose 10 meals a week, which I was very happy about. There are not really any cooking facilities at the residence halls. At the campus apartments there is a common area with a kitchen.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is not cheap. But it is easy. The rooms are furnished you only have to buy sheets, towels and stuff like that. The roommates will probably be freshmen. It is a little unfortunate that your roommates are not the same age as you. In my experience it was possible to find friends outside the dorms which made the arrangement fine.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
The process of finding housing was very stressful and housing was very expensive no matter what I chose. 
If you do not want to live on campus, you can try to find housing yourself. I recommend looking at facebok groups. There are different groups, they are all called something like “Isla Vista housing” or “UCSB housing”. Do not expect a single room. It is normal to share a room with 1-2 others. Also be careful with fraud at the facebook groups.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is super easy. I got all the classes I wanted. However, I will recommend taking one more class than you need to and after the first week drop the one class you like the least. That is the common way to do it at UCSB.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
You sign up for classes at their website called GOLD. At the website you can find information about when you can sign up. At that time be prepared for which classes you want to take. Be aware that some classes fill up quickly. Make sure that the classes don't overlap in the weekly schedule and the exam week. All the information about the classes you can find if you look up UCSB course catalog on google and then search for courses by subject area. 
If the class have prerequisites, you can email the department that offers the class to get a sign up code. 
Therefor look up in good time which classes you wish for (make sure to have a plan b), if any prerequisites e-mail the department and be ready by the time you have your sign up timeslot.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: If you write to the department, they will help you.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted. I did experience that in the first week of class I changed my mind and wanted another course. This made everything a little difficult. I could just have signed up for four classes and tried them all out and sign off on one of them.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be prepared for the sign up timeslot with prerequisites, plan B and consider adding an extra course in case you don't like one of the classes you have chosen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I was happy with my classes. I chose only undergraduate classes, but the upper division of undergraduate classes. The classes have numbers and classes with numbers higher than 100 are for higher level. Some were not so challenging, but then I had more time to go experience Santa Barbara.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There was no time for doing assignments or homework problem in class. It is expected of you to do it at home. I found it much more fun and rewarding to sit together with one or two other students after class and go over the homework together. I will therefor recommend finding a friend in each class.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Biophysics and Biomolecular Materials
Introduction to Scientific Computation
Geophysical Time-Series Analysis
Geophysics
Geophysics (Seismology)
Global Warming

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Depending on your area of interest all the classes I took, I really liked. My favorite was the Geophysical Time-Series Analysis. If You take this class, you can become very good at Fourier Transformation. I also really liked the Global Warming course. Not that much heavy physics or mathematics in the class, but a lot of interesting point on global warming and a good professor.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: It costed more than I expected to establish myself with towels and sheets and so on.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing was very expensive. It took up most of my budget.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There are a lot of things happening at UCSB. You must find them yourself. For example, they have choirs and they did a musical. You can also try and join their soccer team. 
I joined the Excursion club which cost about 30 dollars for three months. Here you can borrow their surf boards, kayaks, wet suits, climbing equipment and a whole lot of other stuff. They also arrange field trips each week to go skiing, hiking or paint the sunset.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend joining the Excursion club.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Find some good friends you feel comfortable with and arrange a weekend trip to San Francisco, Los Angeles or similar. It is easy enough to rent a car. California is a big place with a lot of things to see.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was all fine. I arrived a couple of days before and lived at a hotel. I got to know some of the other exchange students from Denmark and we met up to go explore a bit of Santa Barbara before the school started. After that I can only recommend talking to as many people as you can. Generally, I find that most of the people you will meet are friendly and wants to talk.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It really helped me bonding with people in my classes. Starting the conversation with homework and then go to parties together or drink smoothies from Blenders (if it is still there – It is really good) or something else. There are also lot of eateries nearby campus which is fun to try with some locals.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: It was not so much any cultural differences that was challenging. It was much more being able to small talk in English that was challenging for me, but after a while I got over it. The best solution to that is to just leap into it and talk to everyone you meet.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are very friendly and open. Most people loved to talk even though we did not know each other yet. In that way it made it easy to get in touch with new people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Make friends with people in your classes. It will help you with both the studies and the social life. 
Join clubs and go on trips. It is a great possibility to experience another culture and environment.
Prepare as much as you can from home, so you can relax and enjoy this great experience. It goes by so fast.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The buss was free for students at UCSB, which was nice and made it easy to go downtown. I bought a used bike which I was really happy about and I sold it just before I left.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met in class. I found friends in my field of interest whom I still talk to.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge for my exchange was finding housing. I will recommend starting early by joining facebook group for UCSB housing and looking at campus housing website.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer:
Remember to enjoy the experience it is a great and one-of-a-kind experience. 
Another tip: It is nice to have mobile connection from the beginning. I used MintMobile. With that you can download an electronic sim card before arriving in California.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
